 Talarico takes early lead over Paxton in Texas Senate race as results roll in
 If Talarico maintains his lead and is declared the winner, he will be the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. 
 Andrew Schneider | Posted on November 3, 2026, 4:08 PM (Last Updated: November 3, 2026, 7:51 PM ) 
 Share
 Facebook 
 Twitter/X 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Yfat Yossifor | KERA / Composite Photo U.S. Senate candidates James Talarico and Ken Paxton are both campaigning on affordability and access to the American Dream. 
 Democrat State Rep. James Talarico held an early lead Tuesday night against Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton in the race for Texas' next U.S. senator as the first results began coming in. 
 Loading…
 Sign up for the Hello, Houston! daily newsletter to get local reports like this delivered directly to your inbox. 
 As of 7:45 p.m., it was still too early to call the race, with most Election Day ballots still needing to be counted. 
 If Talarico maintains his lead and is declared the winner, he will be the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. 
 Talarico, a four-term state lawmaker from Austin, was tied or leading in most statewide polls since mid-summer. He led Paxton by a wide margin in fundraising for most of the year, although conservative super PACs allied to the attorney general offset that advantage with heavy spending on advertising in the final two months of the campaign. 
 Talarico first garnered attention in 2018 by flipping the heavily Republican House District 50, which had voted for Donald Trump for president two years earlier. A former San Antonio middle-school teacher and a Presbyterian seminarian, Talarico focused heavily on education issues and staunchly opposed efforts to inject religion into the public-school system. 
 He was one of the most vocal opponents of a law requiring the display of an explicitly Protestant translation of the Ten Commandments in all public-school classrooms, which is now subject to multiple federal lawsuits 
 Paxton defeated incumbent U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in a primary runoff election earlier this year to capture the Republican nomination after receiving a last-minute endorsement from President Donald Trump. 
 Paxton was first elected to the Texas House of Representatives in 2002, and he was elected to the state senate in 2012. Since 2015, he has served as the state's attorney general, extending the scope of its power in that time. 
 Throughout his campaign, Paxton has battled negative perceptions of his own record related to past scandals involving his alleged corruption in office and his ongoing divorce from state Sen. Angela Paxton over his alleged marital infidelities. 
 In 2023, the Texas House of Representatives impeached Paxton for alleged corruption, but he was ultimately acquitted by the Texas Senate.
